svg.aria-label: Four of the load balancing strategies a broker can use, each with three clients, the broker and servers A, B and C. Round robin sends requests to servers in a fixed order, A, B, C, then A again. Weighted round robin gives server A weight 3, B weight 2 and C weight 1, so A gets three requests, B two and C one in each cycle. Least connections sends a new request to the server with the fewest active connections: server A has 5, server B has 2 and server C has 8, so the request goes to server B. Consistent hashing routes key A to server A, key B to server B and key C to server C, because a hash of the request key picks the server and the same key always routes to the same server
svg.text: Load balancing strategies in broker architecture
Four of the strategies the broker can use: pick a server in order, by weight, by current connections, or by a key hash.
Requests are sent to servers in a fixed order:
A → B → C → A and repeat.
Servers with higher weights receive more requests,
for example, A gets 3x, B gets 2x, C gets 1x.
